frequency_question: How often do threatened sweeping executive tariffs on integrated partner sectors actually reach implementation rather than being superseded by negotiated deferrals within the announced window?
membership_rule: Includes explicit executive announcements of sweeping sectoral tariffs (>=25%) against close integrated trade partners (Canada, Mexico, China) where a specific implementation date is set within 1 year. Excludes routine antidumping/countervailing duty administrative findings.

cases.name: Trump Steel and Aluminum Section 232 Tariffs (Canada/Mexico exemptions then application)

coverage_note: 3 named major recent presidential tariff threat cycles involving major partners.
known_gaps: Historical frequency is heavily dependent on the specific administration's bargaining style.
skeleton: Threatened major trade restriction episodes with explicit deadlines categorized by whether they resulted in implemented tariffs or negotiated suspensions.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 3 major distinct escalation cycles yielding a baseline implementation rate of approximately 67% for direct executive trade threats.
validity_reason: Valid through the current presidential term as trade negotiation mechanics and executive authority under Section 232/301 remain constant.
